body_markdown:
## Key Points


- Judge a vibration sensor by the diagnosis behind it: whether an alert names the fault and its severity on the machines you run.
- Tractian Smart Trac Ultra pairs vibration and ultrasound in one IP69K-rated wireless sensor, so one device covers washdown and classified areas.
- Before signing with a service-led vendor, get frequency range, battery life and enclosure ratings in writing.


A good vibration sensor for a plant is the one that detects bearing, imbalance and misalignment faults early on the machines you run, survives the environment, and gives your team a clear next step. Industrial teams now choose between wireless sensors that feed a software platform, handheld meters used on routes, and bare accelerometers wired into a data acquisition system. Learn more about[vibration analysis](https://tractian.com/en/glossary/vibration-analysis) .


This comparison covers the first group, wireless sensors for continuous condition monitoring, from four vendors: Tractian, AssetWatch, Waites and Augury.


## What Makes a Vibration Sensor Worth Buying?


A worthwhile vibration sensor measures vibration across a frequency range wide enough to catch early bearing defects, mounts firmly on the machine, and keeps running for years without a battery change. Six criteria separate one sensor from another:


- Frequency range and sampling: early bearing wear shows up at higher frequencies, so a narrow range can miss it.
- **Triaxial measurement:** three axes help tell imbalance, misalignment and looseness apart.
- **Battery life:** ask how many years a battery lasts at your planned sampling rate, and weigh[battery-powered and wired vibration sensors](https://tractian.com/en/blog/battery-powered-vs-wired-vibration-sensors-choosing-the-right-monitoring-approach) against each other.
- **Wireless range and gateway:** check line of sight versus range through walls and equipment.
- **Enclosure and certification:** washdown areas, dust and hazardous locations need matching ingress and area ratings.
- **Diagnosis and service model:** an alert that names the fault and the severity saves hours compared with a raw spectrum, and too many unranked alerts cause[alert fatigue](https://tractian.com/en/glossary/alert-fatigue) .


## Tractian Smart Trac Ultra


### Best for


Plants that want their own technicians and reliability engineers to see diagnosed faults in one platform, including washdown and hazardous areas.


### Overview


[Tractian Smart Trac Ultra](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/ultrasonic-sensor) is a wireless vibration sensor for rotating equipment that also records temperature, RPM and ultrasound from the same mounting point.


Readings go to the Tractian[condition monitoring platform](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/condition-monitoring) , where[Auto Diagnosis](https://tractian.com/en/resources/videos/auto-diagnosis) matches them to likely failure modes on motors, pumps, fans, gearboxes and compressors. Adding ultrasound to vibration gives an early read on bearing friction and lubrication, useful for[condition-based maintenance](https://tractian.com/en/glossary/condition-based-maintenance) programs that grease on evidence instead of a calendar.


- **Install:** each sensor mounts with adhesive or drill-and-tap and goes live within minutes, and CMRP and CAT-certified specialists help with installation and train the team.
- **Hazardous areas:** Smart Trac Ultra is IP69K rated and[hazardous-location certified for ATEX, IECEx, and NFPA 70 Class 1, 2, and 3 (Division I)](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/sensor-specifications) .
- **Integrations:** alerts flow into CMMS, ERP and EAM systems such as Maximo and Oracle through[Tractian integrations](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/integrations) .


### Key features


- Vibration, trend and spectrum sampling up to 64 kHz.
- Battery life of 3 to 5 years, depending on configuration and environment.
- Radio reach of up to 3,300 ft in open line of sight and 330 ft through obstacles.
- A bearing library of more than 70,000 models plus RPM detection, used to pinpoint fault frequencies.
- Severity-ranked[failure detection](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/failure-detection) alerts with a root cause and next steps for the technician.


### Customer results and industries


- [Chemical](https://tractian.com/en/industry/chemical) **:** CP Kelco, a maker of nature-based ingredients, avoided 84 hours of downtime, including a major unbalance incident on a dryer bearing. Gautam Sane, Senior Reliability Engineer, points to the real-time reliability metrics and failure mode detail, and explains[why CP Kelco chose to partner with Tractian](https://tractian.com/en/resources/videos/why-cp-kelco-chose-to-partner-with-tractian) .
- [Food and beverage](https://tractian.com/en/industry/food-and-beverage) **:** In[Danone](https://tractian.com/en/case-studies/danone) dairy production, Tractian AI flagged a rising vibration profile on a homogenizer pulley, an early sign of possible misalignment. The planned repair avoided $40K in maintenance costs and an estimated $120K to $600K in commercial impact.


Before a plantwide rollout, check the[7 things to prove before scaling a machine monitoring pilot](https://tractian.com/en/blog/7-things-to-prove-before-scaling-a-machine-monitoring-pilot) .


### Tractian pricing for a vibration sensor program


Tractian scopes a vibration sensor program to your assets: which machines are critical, how they fail, and how many sensors it takes to catch those faults early. A Tractian specialist turns that into a custom quote, so start by sharing the list of machines you want covered.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- Which bearing or misalignment fault have you caught on a machine like mine, and what did the alert say? Auto Diagnosis maps signals to failure modes, and each alert carries a root cause and next steps.
- What does ultrasound add on my critical rotating assets? With 64 kHz sampling and ultrasound in the same housing, one device covers bearing wear and lubrication condition.
- How long until our first sensors report? Mounting takes minutes per sensor, batteries last 3 to 5 years, and certified specialists support the rollout.
- Will one sensor model work in both washdown rooms and classified zones? The IP69K rating and hazardous-location certification above cover both.
- Who in my industry can confirm the results? Start with the chemical and food and beverage references above.


## AssetWatch


### Best for


Companies that want a managed program where the vendor does most of the analysis.


### Overview


AssetWatch delivers condition monitoring as a managed service. Vibration, temperature, electrical and oil analysis data go to one platform, and a person reviews each finding before it reaches the customer.


### Key features


- One subscription with no CapEx, plus a $199 trial.
- Install in about one day, with a median of about 3 days to the first actionable alert.
- Route-based and continuous vibration, electrical monitoring and oil analysis.
- Alerts that state what was detected, why it matters and what to do next.
- A Condition Monitoring Engineer, Asset Reliability Technician and Customer Success Manager assigned per account.


AssetWatch does not publish sensor frequency range, battery life or wireless range.


### Pricing


Beyond the $199 trial, AssetWatch does not publish subscription prices. Because the sensors stay part of the service, weigh the multi-year subscription against buying sensors outright. Learn more about[CapEx versus OpEx budgeting for sensor programs](https://tractian.com/en/blog/capex-or-opex-budgeting-for-condition-monitoring) .


### Questions to ask before you buy


- What are the sensor frequency range, battery life and wireless range? Without these figures in writing, a hardware comparison has nothing to check against. On r/IndustrialMaintenance, a maintenance user wrote in[a thread on AssetWatch vibration sensors](https://www.reddit.com/r/IndustrialMaintenance/comments/1s90y9s/assetwatch_vibration_sensors/) that such sensors are far less accurate than a high-end vibration tech's equipment and typically measure a single location, so ask for accuracy evidence on your assets.
- Do your technicians get the raw vibration data and the reasoning behind each call? With an analyst between the alert and your team, ask for the typical time from detection to alert.
- How does the price change as you add assets and sites? Ask what happens to the hardware and your data history if you leave.


## Waites


### Best for


Companies that want wireless vibration sensors in a stainless steel case with analyst-reviewed data.


### Overview


Waites offers wireless vibration sensors in a 316 stainless steel case. They monitor full-spectrum vibration and temperature with a line of sight radio range of roughly 3,000 feet.


### Key features


- ImpactVUE technology, which helps detect early bearing and lubrication issues.
- Vibration analysts and reliability engineers review incoming data around the clock, together with machine learning.
- Tethered sensors and network hardware alongside the wireless line.


The sensors do not measure RPM or ultrasound, and Waites does not state[hazardous-area certifications such as ATEX](https://tractian.com/en/competitors/tractian-vs-waites) , battery life or platform integrations. Variable-speed machines are harder to read without RPM, and plants in oil and gas or chemicals need the area rating in writing before mounting.


### Pricing


Waites quotes pricing on request and keeps no public list.


### What to confirm with Waites


Ask what battery life applies at your sampling interval, since a replacement plan for hundreds of sensors cannot be budgeted without it. Ask which parts of the diagnosis are automated and which wait on an analyst, including response times during shift changes and weekends. Then confirm how a diagnosed fault becomes a work order in your maintenance system, because no integrations are stated.


## Augury


### Best for


Companies that want an industrial AI platform that includes machine health.


### Overview


Augury sells industrial AI agents and continuous machine monitoring across assets. Its Machine Health sensors capture triaxial vibration, temperature and magnetic flux, and its signals also include ultrasound.


### Key features


- Cloud analysis that combines AI diagnostics with human review.
- Alerts that state fault severity, root cause and a recommended action.
- AI agents that work on connected operations data.
- Alerts sent to a connected CMMS or EAM, with no native work order management published.
- Endpoint 3XS:[IP67](https://tractian.com/en/competitors/tractian-vs-augury) rating, up to 3 years of battery life, about 50 ft of in-plant range and a 60-minute data capture standard.
- A mobile app limited to sensor installation.


Confirm these figures with Augury before you plan gateway placement.


### Pricing


Augury quotes each customer separately with no public price list, which makes year-two and multi-site costs hard to compare, so request a multi-year quote.


### What to confirm with Augury


Augury does not publish a frequency range, so ask for it in writing along with battery life at your sampling rate. Ask how sensors, software and services are bundled in the quote. Because alerts depend on a connected CMMS or EAM, ask Augury to demonstrate the alert-to-work-order handoff in your own system.

## How to Choose a Vibration Sensor


Start with your most critical rotating assets, then work through this checklist before you request a quote:


- List the machines, their speeds and the failure modes that have cost you downtime.
- Get frequency range, sampling options and battery life in writing for the interval you plan to run.
- Confirm the enclosure and area rating for your washdown, dust or hazardous zones.
- Walk the site for gateway placement and check range with obstacles.
- Decide whether your team wants a managed service or direct access to diagnosed faults. Tractian engineers can also review alerts when a team wants a second opinion.
- Pilot on a small set of assets and compare the alerts against what technicians find on inspection.


Track missed faults during the pilot as well. In[an r/IndustrialMaintenance thread on vibration analysis for condition monitoring](https://www.reddit.com/r/IndustrialMaintenance/comments/1sjtf1u/vibration_analysis_for_condition_monitoring/) , one maintenance user reported that around 50% of respondents still experienced failures despite vibration-based predictive maintenance.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Which vibration sensor suits predictive maintenance?


The right sensor depends on the machine. For rotating assets such as motors, pumps, fans and gearboxes, look for a triaxial wireless sensor with a frequency range wide enough for bearing faults, multi-year battery life and a rating that fits the environment. Then check how the platform turns the data into a diagnosis, using[predictive maintenance](https://tractian.com/en/glossary/predictive-maintenance) practice as the yardstick.


### What is the difference between a vibration sensor and a vibration meter?


A vibration meter is a handheld instrument used on routes, so it captures a reading when someone walks by. A permanently mounted vibration sensor measures continuously or on a schedule and sends data to software, which lets a team see a trend building between rounds.


### Do I need a triaxial vibration sensor?


A triaxial sensor measures vibration in three directions, which helps separate faults such as imbalance, misalignment and looseness that show up more strongly in different directions. Single-axis sensors can work on simpler assets, so match the choice to the machine.


### How long do wireless vibration sensor batteries last?


It depends on sampling rate, distance to the gateway and temperature. Smart Trac Ultra battery life is 3 to 5 years. For other vendors, request the figure for your own sampling schedule.


### Should I choose a managed service or a self-service platform?


A managed service suits teams without in-house vibration analysts, because the vendor reviews alerts for them. A self-service platform with automated diagnosis suits teams that want their own technicians to see the data and the reasoning. Ask each vendor how your team builds its own skills over time.
